newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Strong growth seen in Asian wheat consumption-USDA.
newsitem.headline: Strong growth seen in Asian wheat consumption-USDA.

text.p: Asian wheat consumption is likely to grow rapidly over the next few years and the U.S. wants to secure a large chunk of the market, a senior U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) analyst said on Monday.

Lee Schatz, deputy director of analysis in the Grain and Feed division of the Foreign Agriculture Service in the USDA, told a conference that robust economic growth, rising population and urbanisation would boost wheat trade in Asia.

Of the estimated 27 cities which are likely to have populations of 10 million by the year 2015, 17 will be in Asia. "The challenge is to meet the needs of those cities. There's no way to change that trend," he said.
"At the top of the list is Southeast Asia...we're now seeing Southeast Asian imports kicking in."

Indonesia and the Philippines are already the two leading buyers of U.S. wheat. Jakarta buys about four million tonnes while Manila purchases around 2.1 million tonnes of wheat a year, traders and analysts said.
The two countries are in the top 10 leading buyers of U.S. wheat, grain officials said. Southeast Asia grows almost no wheat and depends on imports for up to 95 percent of its supply.

Schatz said strong Asian growth will underpin a sharp expansion in world wheat trade and that the U.S. would need to produce a near record crop in the 2005/06 (June/May) marketing year to lock up a healthy share of the market.
"We want half the growth in world trade in the years ahead," he said. Wheat imports would easily reach several million tonnes, he added.
